newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's OM to launch London paper and pulp bourse.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's OM to launch London paper and pulp bourse.

text.p: Swedish options and derivatives group OM Gruppen AB said on Thursday it planned to open a bourse for timber, pulp and paper products in London which would help the industry to cope with wild fluctuations in product prices.

The PULPEX bourse, due to come on line in the first half of 1997, would ultimately serve as a marketplace and clearing house for all pulp and paper products, but the first commodity to be traded on is to be pulp.

"Through the establishment of PULPEX, London will have a commodities bourse for forest products which complements existing bourses for oil, metals and 'softs' (coffee, sugar and cocoa)," OM said in a statement.
PULPEX is the result of a three-year project run in cooperation between OM and representatives of the forest industry, the company said.
Huge swings in the price of pulp over the past few years have made pulp producers' profitability unpredictable and has made investing in new production capacity a risky business.

Softwood pulp prices have been as low as $400 per tonne and as high as $1,000 over the past few years, and the profits of forestry groups in the Nordic region and elsewhere have fluctuated accordingly.
"Without the ability to hedge prices, changes in the world market price for pulp have had an immediate impact on players' profitability," OM said.

Global production of pulp is now around 200 million tonnes per year, of which around 20 percent or 40 million tonnes is sold on the spot market. At current prices, this puts the value of spot market turnover at around $25 billion.
PULPEX's clearing operation will be covered by the parent company guarantee issued by OM Gruppen to its wholly-owned bourses and clearing organisations.
The bourse's head office will be based in London.
